source.title: Impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on patient outcomes: a network meta-analysis
source.source_type: systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of double-blind randomized controlled trials

atoms.canonical_statement: The review evaluated individual SGLT2 inhibitors across patients with and without diabetes mellitus, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease, emphasizing mortality, cardiovascular, kidney, and safety outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A comprehensive network meta-analysis comparing the effects of individual sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors on patients with and without comorbidities including diabetes mellitus (DM), heart failure (HF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD) has not been previously conducted.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov through March 28, 2023 and restricted inclusion to English-language double-blind randomized trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We conducted a comprehensive search for RCTs published before March 28, 2023 in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov, and only retrieved double-blind trials so that placebo groups could be included in the NMA.

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible studies enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with or without diabetes, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease; administered an SGLT2 inhibitor; used a non-SGLT2-inhibitor control; and reported prespecified mortality, cardiovascular, kidney-progression, or acute-kidney-injury outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We considered RCTs to be eligible if they met the following criteria: (a) population: adult patients (≥18 years old) with/without DM, HF, and CKD separately; (b) intervention: patients administrated SGLT2 inhibitors; (c) control group as patients who did not take SGLT2 inhibitors; (d) outcome: risks of all-cause mortality, CV death, CV death or HHF, kidney function progression, and AKI.

population.label: Adults with or without DM, HF, or CKD
exclusion_criteria: missing SGLT2 inhibitor or outcome information

atoms.canonical_statement: Fourteen randomized trials including 75,334 participants were included; 40,956 participants received an SGLT2 inhibitor and 34,378 did not.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A total of fourteen trials with 75,334 patients were analyzed. Among these, 40,956 had taken SGLT2 inhibitors and 34,378 had not.

atoms.canonical_statement: The active treatments evaluated were dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, canagliflozin, ertugliflozin, and sotagliflozin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We divided the five SGLT2 inhibitors into two groups based on their relative SGLT2 selectivity: highly selective SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin) and less selective SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin and sotagliflozin).

atoms.canonical_statement: Placebo/non-SGLT2-inhibitor control groups formed the common comparator network; the included trials contained no direct randomized comparisons between two active SGLT2 inhibitors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No evaluation of inconsistency between the direct and indirect effects was required since no direct comparisons between any two SGLT2 inhibitors in the included trials.

atoms.canonical_statement: The efficacy outcomes included all-cause death, cardiovascular death, cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization, major adverse cardiac events, kidney-function progression, acute kidney injury, and renal-specific composite outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Outcomes were all-cause death, CV death, CV death or HHF, MACEs, kidney function progression, AKI, renal-specific composite outcomes and diabetic complications.

atoms.canonical_statement: Three-point major adverse cardiac events were defined as cardiovascular death, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 3-points MACEs encompassed CV death, ischemic stroke or myocardial infarction.

outcome.definition: cardiovascular death, ischemic stroke, or myocardial infarction

atoms.canonical_statement: The renal composite outcome was defined as kidney progression plus acute kidney injury.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The renal composite outcome was defined as a composite of kidney progression and AKI.

outcome.definition: kidney progression and acute kidney injury

atoms.canonical_statement: Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2, and confidence in network estimates was assessed with CINeMA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We employed the Risk of Bias tool 2.0 to assess the possible biases of the enrolled studies. We used the CINeMA (Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis) web application to assess the certainty of evidence.

atoms.canonical_statement: The network meta-analysis used frequentist random-effects methods in R 4.2.2, with MetaInsight for network maps and SUCRA for treatment ranking.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Initially, a set of network analysis was conducted using R (version 4.2.2, R Project for Statistical Computing) software, and frequentist statistics was used for the meta-analysis to approach a random-effect NMA.

atoms.canonical_statement: Trial sequential analysis used a two-sided significance level of 0.05, 90% power, and O’Brien-Fleming alpha-spending boundaries to assess cumulative evidence for selected outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The conventional non-superiority boundaries were set at significance levels of 0.05 and a power of 90%. The α-spending boundaries were calculated using the O’Brien-Fleming procedure.

atoms.canonical_statement: Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots and Egger’s test.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We checked publication bias using funnel plots along with the Egger’s test.

atoms.canonical_statement: The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO as CRD42022361906.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The systematic review protocol was meticulously planned in advance and registered in PROSPERO [CRD42022361906].

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors classified dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin as highly selective SGLT2 inhibitors and canagliflozin and sotagliflozin as less selective SGLT2 inhibitors for subgroup analyses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: highly selective SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin) and less selective SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin and sotagliflozin)

atoms.canonical_statement: The study-selection process identified 1,224 records, removed 721 duplicates, and included 14 randomized trials after full-text exclusions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Records identified from databases (n = 1,224)

population.label: Records identified by the systematic search

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Records identified from databases (n = 1,224); duplicates excluded (n = 721); studies included in meta-analysis (n = 14)

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains for all 14 included trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The result showed low risk of bias in all domains for all 14 included trials.

atoms.canonical_statement: For diabetes and non-diabetes analyses, funnel plots and Egger’s test were reported as showing no apparent publication bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For DM/non-DM data, funnel plot and Egger’s test were used to check the publication bias, and no apparent publication bias was observed.

atoms.canonical_statement: Because the network contained no direct active-drug comparisons, the authors did not perform a direct-versus-indirect inconsistency evaluation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No evaluation of inconsistency between the direct and indirect effects was required since no direct comparisons between any two SGLT2 inhibitors in the included trials.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the authors’ qualitative safety summary, canagliflozin was associated with a higher lower-limb amputation risk among patients with diabetes, and ertugliflozin was associated with higher urinary-tract-infection risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: canagliflozin was linked to a higher risk of lower limb amputation ... For the other diabetic complications, ertugliflozin was linked to a higher risk of UTI than other SGLT2 inhibitors.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the supplement’s CANVAS study summary, canagliflozin was reported to increase amputation risk versus placebo with HR 1.97 and a printed 95% CI of 1.41-1.75; the printed interval does not contain the reported point estimate.

source_anchor.supplement: Summary of features in each study - CANVAS Program
source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: canagliflozin users also had an increased risk of amputation 1.97 (95% CI: 1.41 to 1.75) than placebo users.

atoms.canonical_statement: Baseline subgroup data were incomplete across trials, creating potential verification bias and differences in placebo-group baseline risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: information on baseline characteristics in each subgroup was incomplete among the included studies, leading to verification bias and different baseline risks in each placebo group.

atoms.canonical_statement: Definitions of chronic kidney disease and heart failure varied across trials, increasing imprecision and limiting comparability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the CKD and HF definitions varied between each article, leading to imprecision.

atoms.canonical_statement: Subgroup outcome data were unavailable for some outcomes, follow-up duration varied, and competing mortality risk may bias event estimates.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we could not retrieve certain subgroup patient data for each outcome, and the follow-up period varied between the studies. Consequently, there was a competing risk of death.

atoms.canonical_statement: Some included randomized trials were terminated early or changed endpoints, potentially introducing survivor bias and power limitations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: some randomized trials terminated early and changed their clinical endpoints, which may lead to survival bias and power failure.

atoms.canonical_statement: Only one ertugliflozin trial was available, limiting precision for ertugliflozin comparisons.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only one study on ertugliflozin was retrieved, which may weaken the precision.

atoms.canonical_statement: The analysis combined multiple doses rather than restricting comparisons to fixed doses, which could confound active-drug comparisons.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we did not limit the dosage of SGLT2 inhibitors, and we combined all different doses, which may be a confounding factor in the comparisons.

atoms.canonical_statement: The high-versus-low SGLT2-selectivity grouping was an artificial analytic classification and may introduce indication bias.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we artificially categorized dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin as highly selective ... The classification may lead to an indication bias.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors cautioned that several analyses remained inconclusive because too few randomized trials were available and that further trials were needed for the non-heart-failure cardiovascular composite.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: some results were inconclusive due to the lack of sufficient RCTs. According to TSA, more studies with non-HF patients are required to attain the required information size for the composite of CV outcomes.

atoms.canonical_statement: The placebo-connected network does not reflect real-world active-treatment choice and leaves active-agent comparisons indirect.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we only compared SGLT2 inhibitors to placebo; however, this may not reflect real-world practice.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that dapagliflozin and empagliflozin lowered kidney and cardiovascular composite outcomes versus placebo, while canagliflozin lowered kidney and cardiovascular composite outcomes but carried a higher limb-amputation signal in patients with diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin were associated with lower risks of kidney events and composite CV outcomes than placebo. Canagliflozin was associated with lower risks of kidney progression and composite CV outcomes, but a higher risk of limb amputation compared with placebo in the patients with DM.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that less selective SGLT2 inhibitors had the best cardiovascular composite outcomes among patients with heart failure, including comparisons against highly selective SGLT2 inhibitors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the HF patients, less selective SGLT2 inhibitors were associated with the best CV composite outcomes, even outperforming highly selective SGLT2 inhibitors.
